Let's build the game. File plan: index.html, game.js, style.css, README.txt (Russian README).

Key features:
- Terrain: procedurally generated rolling hills with steep slopes and jumps (gaps).
- Car: chassis + 2 wheels with suspension, wheel-terrain contact, stable physics.
- Controls: right/left or D/A for gas/brake, touch pedals, P for pause, R for instant restart, sound toggle.
- Fuel consumption, refueling pickups (fuel cans).
- Coins.
- Distance, best record saved in localStorage, garage upgrades also saved locally.
- Camera follows.
- Game over on fuel out or rollover.
- Debug DOM element with id="debug" showing distance, speed, fuel, coins, game state, car angle.

Physics approach: I need stable, reliable physics that don't blow up. Let me think through a simple, robust approach.

Terrain: height function y(x) built from segments — smooth noise + occasional jumps (cliff steps). Use value noise with increasing amplitude/frequency (progressively steeper). Jumps: as a step in height. For wheel contact, compute terrain height at wheel x, place wheel at terrain height + wheel radius, and compute terrain normal.

Simplest robust model: rigid car body with 2 wheels connected via spring-damper suspension along body normal. Wheel position = chassis attachment point + suspension offset along body's down direction. Wheel touches ground: if wheel y (canvas y, down positive) > terrainHeight(wheel x) + radius, compression = penetration. Apply spring force upward on wheel, transfer to body.

Alternatively, simulate wheels as particles constrained to terrain, and connect body to wheels with springs. This is a common approach and reasonably stable.

Let me design physics carefully:

Body: position (x, y) center, angle θ, angular velocity ω. Mass m, inertia I.
Wheels i=0,1: local anchor points (±wheelbase/2, wheelHeight below center). Suspension: wheel offset along body-local down direction, s_i in [minTravel, maxTravel]. Wheel world position = bodyPos + rotate(anchor, θ) + downDir * s_i.

Forces:
- Gravity on body: m*g.
- For each wheel: wheel effective mass mw. Wheel is pushed along body down-axis by spring k*s and damping, gravity on wheel, ground contact.

Simpler: treat wheels as massless, compute compression directly: desired wheel position is anchor + s0 (rest length). If ground penetrates, compression c = (groundHeight + r - wheelY)... let me define coordinate system: y increases downward (canvas). Terrain height function h(x) returns y of ground surface (larger y = lower on screen). Wheel center at wheelY. Contact when wheelY + r > h(x), i.e., wheel below ground line → penetration depth d = wheelY + r - h(x) > 0. Actually wheel center should be at h(x) - r (above ground, since y is downward). Penetration = wheelY + r - h(x).

Forces on wheel (mass mw): gravity m_w*g (downward = +y), spring from body pushes wheel down: k*(s0 - s) where s = current suspension travel... this is getting complex. Let's simplify:

Wheel as particle with mass mw, position (wx, wy), velocity. Connected to body anchor by spring along body down-axis: spring rest length L0, direction = body down. Spring force magnitude = k*(L0 - s) - damping*ds/dt, pushing wheel away from body if compressed.

Ground contact: if wy + r > h(x): normal force pushes wheel up (−y), along terrain normal n (n = normalized (−slope, −1)? Let me compute: terrain y = h(x). Surface normal pointing up (negative y): n = normalize((-h'(x), -1))? Check: surface is y=h(x); gradient of F(x,y)=y−h(x) is (−h', 1); this points in +y direction (into ground). Up-normal = (h'(x) −? hmm. n_up = normalize((h'(x), -1))? Check flat: h'=0 → (0,-1), up. Good.

Contact: penetration d = wy + r − h(wx) > 0. Apply spring-damper normal force: F = kd*d − cd*d'(damping in normal direction). Use large kd, cap, and clamp wheel to surface if deeply penetrating to avoid explosion (position correction). Also friction: tangential force from gas/brake.

Drive force: apply torque at wheel contact point: tangential direction t = normalize((1, h')) (pointing right, along downhill slope). Gas applies force along +t (drives right, forward). Brake opposes wheel velocity along t.

Friction force: F_f = mu * N * t_dir, limited by traction. Gas force limited by normal force to avoid infinite wheel spin.

Body dynamics: forces from both wheels transmitted to body at anchor points → generates torque. Each wheel spring transmits force along body down-axis: F_spring = (springForce) * downDir. Plus wheel ground forces transmitted through suspension: essentially total force on wheel (ground contact + spring) — treat the wheel spring force as internal, and ground contact forces propagate through spring to body. Simplest: compute spring force on wheel; equal-opposite acts on body at anchor (with torque from anchor offset). Ground contact force on wheel acts on wheel; wheel also has mass. This is standard and works.

To ensure stability: clamp spring force, clamp wheel position above ground (wy = min(wy, h(wx) − r) after integration), clamp velocity, use fixed timestep dt (e.g., 1/120, multiple substeps per frame). Use semi-implicit Euler.

Rollover: track angle; if |angle| > ~2.4 rad (near upside down), and grounded or speed low, start rollover timer; game over after 2 seconds.

Air rotation: when both wheels off ground, apply torque from gas/brake? In Hill Climb Racing, in the air, gas rotates the car forward. So: when airborne, gas/brake applies angular acceleration to body. Yes.

Fuel: consumption proportional to gas usage + small base. Fuel pickups appear on terrain. Fuel 0 → game over (maybe when car is stationary, or immediately). Let's do game over when fuel ≤ 0.

Coins: collectible on ground, add to counter, saved in total coins for garage. Garage upgrades: engine, suspension, fuel tank, tires (grip). Save in localStorage. Garage UI: simple panel with upgrade buttons, costs, coin count. Coins persist across runs.

Game states: menu (garage), playing, paused, gameover. Draw UI on canvas + minimal HTML overlay? Keep everything on canvas, plus debug div. Touch pedals: draw on-screen pedals on canvas, handle pointer events.

Camera: follow car with smoothing, slight lookahead.

Rendering: sky gradient, sun, clouds, hills background (parallax), grass terrain with dirt cross-section, trees, bushes. Car drawn with original graphics: body shape, window, wheels with spokes, rotation.

Sound toggle: WebAudio beeps/engine hum. Simple engine sound: oscillator with pitch based on speed/rpm, toggle button. Keep simple and safe (create audio on user interaction).

Controls: ArrowRight/D = gas, ArrowLeft/A = brake, P pause, R restart, M mute, Enter/G for garage? Keep: from game-over or menu, Space to start.

Debug element: fixed small div in corner, updated every frame with distance, speed, fuel, coins, state, angle.

Files:

index.html: canvas, debug div, minimal CSS link.
style.css.
game.js: everything.
README.txt: Russian, controls.

Double-clicking index.html: localStorage works on file:// in most browsers, so fine.

// ---------- terrain ----------
Deterministic pseudo-random via seeded hash. Terrain defined by function groundY(x). Build incrementally: store anchor points every SEG=60 px, heights via layered sines + random walk + occasional jump steps. Better: precompute array of anchors from x=0 to some length (say 20000, extend as needed). Height: base rolling + amplitude growth with x (progressive difficulty). Jumps: at random intervals add step (drop) — creates launch ramp: ramp up then cliff down.

Implementation: array terrain: for x from -200 to 20000 step 40, store height. Extend when car approaches end. Height generation: h(x) = baseLine + noise. Use smooth noise: value noise with interpolation.

Simpler: generate anchor points sequentially with a seeded RNG:
- h += slope; slope varies smoothly; occasionally big slope segment (climb) then step down (jump).

Let me do: anchor array every 40 px. For each anchor: h_{i+1} = h_i + dh, where dh = smoothNoise-based slope + occasional step. For smoothness, ensure terrain height is continuous at step boundaries (step is a jump in height → vertical cliff). Wheel contact at cliff: wheel crossing cliff edge — handle via interpolation of groundY(x): use smooth interpolation between anchors, except for entries flagged as step, where groundY returns cliff top/bottom. Hmm, tricky for physics; simpler: make jumps as steep ramps (very steep segment over short distance), not actual cliffs. That way groundY(x) is continuous single-valued function, physics simpler, and visually looks like cliff. Use dense anchors (every 20 px) with large dh for jump segments. GroundY(x) = linear interpolation between anchors. Continuous, fine.

Progressive difficulty: slope amplitude grows with distance; occasional "jump" segments: ramp-up slope ~+0.4..0.6 over 60 px, then drop of -0.8 over 20 px.

Terrain function:
```js
const anchors = []; // {x, y}
function ensureTerrain(x) { extend anchors while last.x < x+1500 }
function groundY(x) { find segment via index = (x - x0)/STEP; interpolate }
function groundSlope(x) { (h(x+3)-h(x-3))/6 or segment slope }
```
Anchors start at x=-400 with y = canvas baseline. Terrain y values in world coords, y increases downward.

Seed RNG: mulberry32.

Generation:
```js
function genAnchors() {
  let x = START_X, y = 0; // world coords, y down
  anchors.push({x, y});
  let slope = 0;
  let segCount=0;
  while(...) {
    const d = x / 4000; // difficulty 0..1+
    // smooth noise slope
    slope += (rand()-0.5)*0.02*(1+d); clamp slope to ±(0.15+0.25*d)
    // occasional jump feature
    if (x > 1200 && rng() < 0.03 per anchor) → schedule feature: 4 anchors ramp up slope +0.45, then 2 anchors steep drop -1.2 (looks cliff, still single-valued)
    y += slope * STEP;
    anchors.push({x: x+STEP, y});
  }
}
```
Careful with deterministic generation per run: reseed on restart so same track? Use fixed seed for consistency; fine.

Car:

- Wheel radius r = 18.
- Wheelbase: anchors at (±30, 12) from center (local, y down).

Force on body = −F at anchor → torque = cross(anchorLocal, F_on_wheel_local)? In world: torque += cross(anchorWorld - bodyPos, F_on_wheel).

Rollover detection: normalized angle; if cos(angle) < -0.2 (roof down) → rolloverTimer accumulates; game over after 1.5 s. Reset timer when upright.

Garage: draw panel with upgrade buttons; handle clicks. Buttons defined as rects. Upgrade costs: cost = (level+1)*20 coins? Max 5 levels. Effects: engine → engine force & air torque; suspension → spring k & travel; fuel → capacity; tires → grip mu.

'use strict';
const canvas = document.getElementById('game');
const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d');
const debug = document.getElementById('debug');

// ---- helpers ----
const clamp = (v,a,b)=> v<a?a : v>b?b:v;
function mulberry32(seed){ let a = seed>>>0; return function(){ a |= 0; a = a + 0x6D2B79F5 | 0; let t = Math.imul(a ^ a>>>15, 1 | a); t = t + Math.imul(t ^ t>>>7, 61 | t) ^ t; return ((t ^ t>>>14) >>> 0) / 4294967296; }; }

// ---- save ----
const KEY='hillclimb_save_v1';
let save = {coins:0, best:0, up:{engine:0,susp:0,fuel:0,tires:0}};
function loadSave(){ try{ const s=JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(KEY)); if(s&&s.up) save=s; }catch(e){} }
function storeSave(){ try{ localStorage.setItem(KEY, JSON.stringify(save)); }catch(e){} }
loadSave();

// ---- canvas size ----
let W=800, H=600;
function resize(){ W=window.innerWidth; H=window.innerHeight; canvas.width=W; canvas.height=H; }
window.addEventListener('resize', resize); resize();

// ---- constants ----
const G=1000;
const STEP=24;
const X0=-400;
const R_WHEEL=16;

// ---- terrain ----
let anchors=[], rng=null, genX=0;
let pickups=[];
function initTerrain(seed){
  rng=mulberry32(seed);
  anchors=[]; pickups=[]; genX=X0;
  anchors.push({x:X0,y:-40});
  for(let i=0;i<80;i++) addAnchor(); // fill first ~1900 px
}
let slope=0, featureLeft=0;
function addAnchor(){
  const last=anchors[anchors.length-1];
